Area.evidence_source: Most prisoners either said they did not think about the timing of their act (12, 21%) or that they had no special reason for choosing the timing that they did (24, 43%). This reflected the fact that, as noted above, many acts (24, 40%) were impulsive. Of those prisoners who did choose a time for their suicide attempt, most timed it to coincide with not being checked by staff, especially if they were on an Assessment, Care in Custody and Teamwork (ACCT) document (the formal system for registering and monitoring prisoners thought to be at risk of suicide and self-harm in prisons in England and Wales), which required them to be checked at set intervals of time (e.g. every 15 minutes)
